To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
our method achieves state of the art performance in knowledge graph completion tasks.

(1) we introduce a novel path reasoning approach that combines convolutional neural networks and bidirectional long short time memory (BiLSTMs) with an attention mechanism to predict the missing relations in a knowledge graph; (2) we extend our approach to perform multisteps reasoning to infer missing relations in a graph by repeatedly interacting with an attention module; (3) we evaluate our model on several link prediction tasks and show that our model achieves better performance compared to recent path reasoning methods.

we propose a new approach to knowledge graph reasoning that combines bidirectional LSTM with convolutional neural networks and attention mechanism, and show that it achieves state of the art results for link prediction tasks on multiple knowledge graphs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a novel path-based approach for knowledge graph reasoning.
the development of new approaches for reasoning with knowledge graphs.
developing new methods to improve the quality of knowledge graphs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed approach is able to achieve better performance compared with other methods on the link prediction tasks.
we have proposed a novel method for knowledge graph completion based on path reasoning.

we propose a new approach to knowledge graph completion that integrates convolutional neural networks and bidirectional long short-term memory networks to encode paths between two entities and then uses an attention mechanism to capture the semantic relevance between a candidate relation with each path and to predict whether the candidate relation is valid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new approach that can perform multistep path reasoning for knowledge graph completion.
we propose a new approach that can perform multistep path reasoning in knowledge graphs and achieves state of the art performance on link prediction tasks.
we combine the advantages of path based reasoning and embedding methods and propose a new model for knowledge graph completion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of convolutional neural networks with attention mechanism can be used to perform reasoning in knowledge graphs and can be used as a building block for developing new methods for knowledge graph completion.

path based reasoning can achieve better performance than entity and relation embedding methods, which only focus on direct relations, and it can be further enhanced by combining it with attention mechanism.
a path based approach that combines convolutional operation with BiLSTM and attention module can achieve better performance in link prediction tasks than other state of the art methods.
